title: Confirm the Kyrgyz idiom for release from a moral debt
finding: The source exchange “Halallıq alaydım / Halal olsun” concerns release from a moral debt. Kyrgyz uses “ыраазычылыгын алмакмын” and “Мен сизге ыраазымын”. These can read as reciprocal gratitude; the cultural use of expressions of رضا/ыраазылык needs a native Kyrgyz editorial decision before calling the passage a mistranslation.
why: The intended closing meaning should be clear to Kyrgyz readers. Literal reading alone is insufficient to rule out an established cultural formula.
recommended_fix: Ask a native Kyrgyz editor whether this exact noun-and-verb combination conveys release from a moral debt in context. If unclear, make it explicit with wording such as “Сиз мага эч нерсе карыз эмессиз, апа. Көңүлүңүз тынч болсун…”. Retain the existing wording if the cultural idiom is confirmed.

title: English moral generalizes angry speech to all speech
finding: The moral begins “A word spoken is like a nail”, whereas the source explicitly limits the warning to words spoken in anger. The next clause assumes that every such word is uttered in anger.
why: The opening generalization is broader than the source and the story’s lesson.
recommended_fix: Begin “A word spoken in anger is like a nail: its mark may remain long after the moment has passed.” Retain the existing final sentence.

title: Chess metaphor describes an impossible promotion
finding: All versions say a pawn can become a king. FIDE article 3.7.3.3 permits promotion to queen, rook, bishop or knight, not king. The moral clearly concerns social status, so the intended statement may be figurative.
why: Readers familiar with chess may interpret the analogy as a factual mistake rather than deliberate poetic licence.
recommended_fix: Choose whether to retain an explicitly figurative social metaphor or use “become a queen” / “become powerful” and revise the parallel wording in all languages. Do not silently change the author’s metaphor.

title: Wolf-story moral introduces deceit absent from the plot
finding: The dog resembles the wolves but guards the shepherd’s flock. No action establishes that it pretends to be the wolves’ ally, lies to them, or acts hypocritically. The morals nevertheless condemn deceit, hypocrisy or a false game.
why: Physical resemblance and different loyalties do not establish deception; the moral draws a stronger conclusion than the narrated events support.
recommended_fix: For author approval, focus the moral on not confusing outward resemblance with shared intentions or allegiance. Alternatively establish an actual deceptive act in the plot. Preserve the approved text and all illustrations until a decision is made.

title: Retelling closely follows The Calf Path without attribution

why: Readers cannot distinguish this adaptation from an original anonymous tale or locate its literary antecedent.

title: Russian and Kyrgyz inline direct speech uses paragraph-style dashes
finding: Twenty-one Russian and eighteen Kyrgyz paragraphs mix running narration with paragraph-style dialogue dashes without enclosing the direct speech in quotation marks. Each language also has an Albrecht Dürer paragraph using a full stop before this inline dash.
why: Both Russian and Kyrgyz punctuation distinguish inline quoted speech from dialogue beginning on a new line. The mixed form makes speaker boundaries less clear and is inconsistent with the rest of the collection.
recommended_fix: For each occurrence, put the direct speech in a separate paragraph beginning with an em dash; preserve the narration before it and every spoken word. Alternatively, use inline «…» quotation marks with the appropriate punctuation. Do not alter valid dashes that interrupt an existing speaker’s sentence.

title: The two predictions are not strictly equivalent
finding: The narrator says both interpretations have the same meaning. One predicts that all loved ones will die before the king; the other says he will have the longest life in his family. Loved ones and family are not necessarily the same group, and greatest lifespan is not necessarily the latest death when ages differ.
why: The parable’s central claim of identical information depends on an ambiguity, even though its intended lesson about tact is clear.
recommended_fix: Completed: aligned the group in both predictions, used outliving rather than greatest lifespan, and updated the narrator’s explanation in all five languages.

title: The Red Dress needs an adaptation credit
finding: All five versions present the dying mother and unworn red dress narrative without identifying a source. The plot appears to adapt Carol Lynn Pearson’s narrative poem “Millie’s Mother’s Red Dress.” Pearson identifies the poem as her work in her published diary and discusses its inspiration in her interview. why: Readers cannot distinguish the project’s retelling from an original anonymous narrative; the literary source and substantial adaptation are obscured.
recommended_fix: Confirm the edition or intermediate source used, compare it with Pearson’s poem, and add a localized adaptation credit in all five versions. Identify project-added moral text separately where appropriate. Do not describe this prose adaptation as a verbatim translation.

title: The planning analogy treats skill as mere chance
finding: The first paragraph allows a ship to arrive thanks to a capable captain, then classifies that arrival as a result of chance. The Azerbaijani, German, Russian and Kyrgyz versions retain this inference; English already avoids the strongest formulation.
why: A deliberate response by a skilled captain is not necessarily accidental. The overstatement weakens an otherwise useful distinction between a repeatable plan and improvised success.
recommended_fix: Replace the chance-only conclusion with “Such success does not demonstrate a reliable system of management.” Keep the argument for planning, while acknowledging skill and adaptation.

title: Equal time allocation can be mistaken for equal lifespans
finding: Four versions describe time as given to everyone in equal measure. Russian more carefully says the measure of time is the same for everyone.
why: In a reflection about the length of life, the wording can imply that everyone receives the same lifespan or usable time, rather than that time passes without regard to status.
recommended_fix: Clarify the intended metaphor: “Time passes regardless of wealth or fame; how much life each of us has is not the same.” Retain the emphasis on valuing the present.

title: Emotional care is contrasted with medicine as a life-prolonging remedy
finding: All five versions of Thoughtfulness say that sometimes life is prolonged by caring words rather than medicine. The passage is literary, but its contrast can also be read as a literal health claim. Public-health evidence supports the importance of social connection; it does not establish this either/or claim.
why: The contrast distracts from the supported message about emotional support and can suggest that care substitutes for treatment. The author should decide whether to retain the metaphor or remove that implication.
recommended_fix: With author approval, keep the emphasis on care without contrasting it with medicine: AZ “Bəzən qəlbə yaxın sözlər, qayğı və mənəvi yaxınlıq insana yaşamaq üçün yeni güc verir.” EN “Sometimes caring words and a sense of closeness give a person renewed strength to carry on.” Translate that intended sense naturally into DE, RU and KY; retain the existing moral.

title: The tragic outcome appears to prove love despite the opposite moral
finding: In every version, the rose understands the depth of the nightingale’s love only after his suicide. The concluding moral explicitly says love must not be proved through self-destruction. The narrative recognition and the moral therefore pull in different directions.
why: A reader can take the plot to mean that death finally secured recognition of love, even though the moral rejects that conclusion. This is an interpretive tension, not an error in translating the legend.
recommended_fix: Ask the author whether the traditional ending must remain. If an adaptation is acceptable, replace the sentence about finally recognizing the depth of love with a sentence emphasizing irreversible loss, for example: “The rose fell silent. Nothing could bring the nightingale or his song back.” Preserve the explicit moral about valuing life and respecting another person’s choice. If the ending must stay, add a brief interpretive transition explaining that the tragedy proves neither love nor a duty to reciprocate.

title: Hope is expressed as a guarantee that every heartfelt wish will be fulfilled
finding: The opening and moral in all five versions present fulfilment of a heartfelt wish as certain. Unlike a general encouragement to hope, the wording leaves no room for an unfulfilled wish. This is an authorial faith statement, not a factual claim this audit can adjudicate.
why: Readers may understand the encouragement as a promise of a particular outcome. The intended meaning needs clarification before an editor can soften it without changing the author’s religious message.
recommended_fix: Ask the author whether the absolute statement is intentional. If the aim is encouragement rather than a guarantee, approve wording such as “Faith can sustain hope even when our wishes are not fulfilled as we expected,” then translate the approved meaning into all five languages. Otherwise retain it explicitly as the author’s reflection; do not invent a scriptural attribution.

title: The moral praises a benefit without addressing the false offer that produces it
finding: In all five versions, the shopkeeper advertises butter she does not sell to induce a competitor to lower its price. The moral celebrates helping others but does not acknowledge that the advertised offer is false.
why: The comic trick and the stated lesson pull in different directions: a reader could take the moral as approval of misleading others whenever the result benefits someone. This is an interpretive tension, not a request to remove humour or a legal conclusion.
recommended_fix: Ask whether the intended lesson is comic ingenuity or generosity. Preserve the joke if desired, but qualify the moral, for example: “The joke celebrates ingenuity and concern for neighbours; in real trade, helping customers should also mean being honest about what we offer.” Translate only after the author approves the intended interpretation.

title: A literary animal analogy reads as an observation of animal behaviour
finding: All five versions of Before You Marry describe spiny animals finding a warming distance without identifying this as a parable. The recognisable literary parallel is Schopenhauer’s porcupine parable in Parerga und Paralipomena, II, chapter 31, §396.
why: The lesson about personal boundaries is clear, but readers are not told that the animal scene is a literary analogy. The text also uses hedgehogs whereas the cited German original uses porcupines.
recommended_fix: Introduce the image explicitly as a parable, for example “In the familiar parable, spiny animals seek enough closeness for warmth without hurting one another.” If crediting Schopenhauer, identify it as an adaptation of his porcupine parable rather than an exact quotation. Keep the marriage advice unchanged.

title: Four Azerbaijani verb forms incorrectly join vaz to keçmək
finding: Four passages use vazkeçmək, vazkeçim, vazkeçdim or vazkeçir as one word. The Azerbaijani orthographic and explanatory dictionaries list the verbal expression as vaz keçmək; other stories already use the spaced form.
why: The joined spellings introduce orthographic errors and inconsistent spelling of the same expression across the collection.
recommended_fix: Change the four verbal forms to “vaz keçmək”, “vaz keçim”, “vaz keçdim” and “vaz keçir” respectively in the Word sources and regenerated site text. Review the lexicalized adjective vazkeçilməz separately; do not perform an unrestricted replacement inside all words.

title: The girl’s line has a redundant second speech tag
finding: The Azerbaijani and Kyrgyz narration introduces the girl’s speech and then redundantly closes the same line with another speech tag. No intervening speaker or action makes the second tag necessary.
why: The repetition makes a simple exchange feel mechanically narrated and interrupts its flow.
recommended_fix: AZ: keep “Çəkinə-çəkinə dedi:” in the introduction; end the spoken line after “pulunu verərik.” Remove “— dedi qız.” and start “Dükançı qızın sözlərindən…” as a new narrative paragraph. KY: keep “Ал тартынып сүйлөдү:” and remove “— деди кыз.” after “акчасын төлөйбүз,” changing that comma to a full stop. Start “Кыздын сөзүн уккан дүкөнчү…” as the next narrative paragraph.

title: German infinitive clauses lack required separating commas
finding: 55 paragraphs omit commas at clause boundaries. Most are initial expanded infinitive clauses; two are clauses introduced by ohne. These were checked individually against the 2024 rules, including the exceptions for unextended infinitives and multi-part predicates.
why: The punctuation does not consistently follow the current German spelling rules and obscures clause boundaries, particularly in longer morals.
recommended_fix: Insert the missing boundary commas in the listed passages. Do not add commas indiscriminately before every zu: bare infinitives and coherent verbal constructions may correctly lack them. Each exact corrected paragraph is stored with the occurrence as suggested_text.

title: The Chinese-proverb label lacks support and overlooks an identifiable earlier source
finding: All five versions label the four kinds of knowing and not knowing as a Chinese proverb. Al-Ghazali’s Book of Knowledge, section VI, records the same four-part saying and attributes it to al-Khalil ibn Ahmad. This establishes a textual parallel, not proof of its ultimate origin; no Chinese textual source has been identified in this audit.
why: The categorical national attribution may mislead readers about the saying’s provenance.
recommended_fix: Replace the categorical Chinese-proverb label with a source note identifying the parallel in al-Ghazali, Book of Knowledge, section VI, attributed there to al-Khalil ibn Ahmad; describe the site version as an adaptation. Alternatively supply an identifiable Chinese source before retaining that label. Do not assert a definitive country of origin from the parallel alone.

title: Cumalı’s poem excerpt is retitled without identifying the original poem

title: Closing reflection paraphrases the Serenity Prayer without identification
finding: The final reflection in all five versions follows the distinctive three-part sequence of the Serenity Prayer: changing what is possible, accepting what is not, and distinguishing the two. It is presented as the narrator’s reflection without a source note.
why: A recognizable borrowed prayer is difficult to trace, unlike the explicitly credited quotations elsewhere in the collection.
recommended_fix: Add a short note identifying the passage as a paraphrase of the Serenity Prayer, commonly attributed to Reinhold Niebuhr. Keep the narrator’s voice, avoid quotation marks implying a verbatim translation, and do not assign an exact composition date without further evidence.

title: German proverb mixes incompatible comparison structures
finding: The repeated proverb combines the finite clause “man schert die Widder” with the infinitive clause “als den Lämmern die Haut abzuziehen”.
why: The two halves of the comparison do not connect smoothly; the opening and concluding quotation repeat the same awkward construction.
recommended_fix: Use the parallel infinitive construction in both places: “Es ist besser, die Widder zu scheren, als den Lämmern die Haut abzuziehen.” Preserve the quotation’s meaning and its deliberate repetition.

title: The empty-boat retelling does not identify its classical parallel
finding: All five versions frame the story as an unnamed teacher’s personal experience. Its central empty-versus-occupied-boat contrast has an identifiable parallel in Zhuangzi, chapter 20. The site’s dawn meditation and first-person teacher narrative are adaptations, not the wording or scene of that passage.
why: Without an adaptation note, readers cannot trace the literary motif or distinguish the modern retelling from the classical text.
recommended_fix: Add a short note that this is a retelling of the empty-boat motif also found in Zhuangzi, chapter 20, The Tree on the Mountain. Retain the current story and moral, and do not claim that its exact teacher narrative is a direct translation of Zhuangzi. Confirm the wording of the credit before editing.

title: English story headings mix title case and sentence case
finding: The complete 255-title inventory contains both title case (for example The Church Bell and A Mother’s Love) and sentence case (for example A prayer for everyone and A mother's lasting lesson), without an evident genre or author distinction. Single-word and proper-name-only headings are neutral; the attached inventory includes them for coverage and does not label each title individually wrong.
why: Both styles are valid English, but alternating between them makes the same collection look inconsistently edited.
recommended_fix: Choose one English heading convention before changing titles. Apply it to all applicable English story headings, preserving proper names, Allah, identifiers and the wording of approved titles. Update generated catalog/search/page headings together if the choice is approved; do not use automatic title-casing that lowercases names or capitalizes every minor word.

status_evidence: Completed on 2026-11-05. Published English story headings use sentence case. Proper names and Allah stay capitalized. Catalog, search, page headings, and illustration title banners were updated together.

title: Purple-jacket tale needs a provenance note distinguishing fiction from documented custom
finding: All versions already frame the account as a tale. However, the Yörük Culture Research Centre at Süleyman Demirel University specifically disputes the historical custom and associates the narrative with Osman Şahin’s literary work. Other modern publications repeat the tradition claim. The competing accounts are not explained on the site.
why: A reader may still infer that the detailed communal divorce procedure is an established historical practice. Existing tale framing reduces, but does not resolve, this source ambiguity.
recommended_fix: Retain the story and its solidarity moral. Add a short note that the historical basis of this account is disputed and that a university research centre links it to literary fiction. Identify the exact Osman Şahin edition/page before giving a definitive adaptation credit; do not present the absence of field evidence as proof that no such practice ever existed.

occurrences.location: az/wisdom-stories/purple-jacket.docx; body paragraph 1 (catalog paragraphs[0]); corresponding site story
occurrences.exact_text: Yörük obaları haqqında danışılan bir rəvayətdə deyilir ki, ərə gedən qızların cehizinə bənövşəyi çəpkən də qoyularmış. Bu qısa üst geyimi sandığın lap dibində saxlanar, qızın onu heç vaxt geyinməyə ehtiyac duymaması arzulanarmış.

occurrences.location: en/wisdom-stories/purple-jacket.docx; body paragraph 1 (catalog paragraphs[0]); corresponding site story
occurrences.exact_text: A tale about the Yörük communities tells of a purple jacket placed among a bride’s belongings. This short traditional garment was kept at the very bottom of her dowry chest, with the hope that she would never need to wear it.

occurrences.location: de/wisdom-stories/purple-jacket.docx; body paragraph 1 (catalog paragraphs[0]); corresponding site story
occurrences.exact_text: Eine Erzählung über die Gemeinschaften der Yörük berichtet von einer violetten Jacke, die einer Braut in die Aussteuer gelegt wurde. Dieses kurze traditionelle Kleidungsstück lag ganz unten in der Truhe — verbunden mit dem Wunsch, dass die junge Frau es niemals würde tragen müssen.

occurrences.location: ru/wisdom-stories/purple-jacket.docx; body paragraph 1 (catalog paragraphs[0]); corresponding site story
occurrences.exact_text: В одном предании о юрюкских поселениях рассказывается, что в приданое невесты клали фиолетовый чепкен — короткую традиционную куртку. Его хранили на самом дне сундука, желая девушке никогда не оказаться в положении, когда придётся его надеть.

occurrences.location: ky/wisdom-stories/purple-jacket.docx; body paragraph 1 (catalog paragraphs[0]); corresponding site story
occurrences.exact_text: Йөрүк конуштары тууралуу айтылган бир уламышта турмушка чыккан кыздын себине кызгылт көк чепкен кошо салышканы баяндалат. Бул кыска сырт кийим сандыктын эң түбүндө сакталып, кыздын аны кийүүгө эч качан муктаж болбошун тилешчү экен.

title: Seven qualified attributions still lack an identifiable original passage
finding: The quotations credited to Ahrar, al-Ghazali, Saadi, Yaşar Kemal, Yunus Emre, Hacı Bektaş Veli and Mehmed II are already cautiously attributed, but the review has not established an original work, edition and passage for their exact wording. Modern repetition or thematic similarity is insufficient to authenticate a quotation. A modern screenwriter’s competing claim to the Yunus wording also remains unverified against the original script.
why: These are unresolved provenance questions, not seven proven false attributions. Readers cannot verify the wording or distinguish a free modern paraphrase from a traceable quotation.
recommended_fix: For each of the seven texts, supply the original passage and translator/adaptor if available. Otherwise decide explicitly to retain a qualified popular-attribution note, or publish as an unattributed maxim with an editorial note. Do not reassign authorship merely from reposts or a news report. Preserve the meaning and identifier.

occurrences.location: az/wisdom-stories/pleasure-of-allah.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Hacə Ubeydullah Əhrara aid edilən bir kəlamda deyilir:
«Allahın rizasına aparan yolları araşdırdım; ən qısa yolun insanların könlünü sevindirmək olduğunu gördüm.
İnsanı Allahın rizasından uzaqlaşdıran yolları araşdırdım; ən təhlükəli yolun könül qırmaq olduğunu gördüm.»

occurrences.location: en/wisdom-stories/pleasure-of-allah.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
A saying attributed to Khwaja Ubaydullah Ahrar reads:
“I explored the paths that lead to Allah’s pleasure and found that the shortest was to bring joy to people’s hearts.
“I explored the paths that lead away from Allah’s pleasure and found that the most dangerous was to wound another person’s heart.”

occurrences.location: de/wisdom-stories/pleasure-of-allah.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Chodscha Ubaidullah Ahrar werden folgende Worte zugeschrieben:
„Ich habe die Wege erkundet, die zu Gottes Wohlgefallen führen, und erkannt: Der kürzeste ist, Menschen eine Freude zu bereiten.
Ich habe die Wege erkundet, die von Gottes Wohlgefallen wegführen, und erkannt: Der gefährlichste ist, einen Menschen im Herzen zu verletzen.“

occurrences.location: ru/wisdom-stories/pleasure-of-allah.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Ходже Убайдуллаху Ахрару приписывают такие слова:
«Я искал пути к благоволению Аллаха и увидел, что самый короткий — радовать людские сердца.
Я искал то, что лишает человека Его благоволения, и увидел, что опаснее всего — ранить чужое сердце».

occurrences.location: ky/wisdom-stories/pleasure-of-allah.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Кожо Убайдуллах Ахрарга таандык деп айтылган накыл сөздө мындай делет:
«Аллахтын ыраазылыгына жеткирген жолдорду изилдедим. Эң кыскасы — адамдардын көңүлүн кубантуу экенин көрдүм.
Адамды Аллахтын ыраазылыгынан алыстаткан жолдорду изилдедим. Эң кооптуусу — бирөөнүн көңүлүн оорутуу экенин көрдүм».

occurrences.location: az/wisdom-stories/honestly-earned-morsel.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Un təzə, su tərtəmiz olsa da, maya xarabdırsa, xəmir yaxşı acımaz. Belə xəmirdən yaxşı çörək də alınmaz.
Gözəl əxlaqlı övlad böyütmək üçün onu halal qazancla əldə edilmiş tikə ilə bəsləmək lazımdır.
— İmam Qəzaliyə aid edilən fikir

occurrences.location: en/wisdom-stories/honestly-earned-morsel.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Even when the flour is fresh and the water pure, dough will not rise properly if the yeast is spoiled. Nor will it make good bread.
To raise a child of good character, nourish them with food earned honestly.
— Attributed to Imam al-Ghazali

occurrences.location: de/wisdom-stories/honestly-earned-morsel.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Auch wenn das Mehl frisch und das Wasser rein ist: Mit verdorbener Hefe geht der Teig nicht richtig auf. Und daraus wird auch kein gutes Brot.
Wer ein Kind zu einem Menschen mit gutem Charakter erziehen möchte, sollte es mit ehrlich verdientem Brot ernähren.
— Imam al-Ghazali zugeschrieben

occurrences.location: ru/wisdom-stories/honestly-earned-morsel.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Даже если мука свежая, а вода чистая, тесто не поднимется как следует, если дрожжи испорчены. И хорошего хлеба из такого теста не получится.
Чтобы вырастить ребёнка с добрым нравом, его нужно кормить хлебом, заработанным честным трудом.
— Мысль, приписываемая имаму аль-Газали

occurrences.location: ky/wisdom-stories/honestly-earned-morsel.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Ун жаңы, суу таптаза болсо да, ачыткы бузук болсо, камыр жакшы көтөрүлбөйт. Андай камырдан жакшы нан да чыкпайт.
Адептүү бала өстүрүү үчүн аны адал эмгек менен табылган оокат менен багуу керек.
— Имам Газалиге таандык деп айтылган ой

occurrences.location: az/wisdom-stories/how-we-treat-people.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
İnsanlarla münasibətində odun qarşısında dayandığın kimi dayan:
Nə çox uzaqlaş ki, soyuqdan donasan, nə də çox yaxınlaş ki, istisindən yanasan.
— Sədi Şiraziyə aid edilən kəlam

occurrences.location: en/wisdom-stories/how-we-treat-people.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Approach your relationships as you would a fire:
Stay too far away, and you will freeze.
Get too close, and you will burn.
— Attributed to Saadi Shirazi

occurrences.location: de/wisdom-stories/how-we-treat-people.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Halte es mit Menschen wie mit dem Feuer:
Bleibst du zu weit weg, frierst du. Kommst du zu nahe, verbrennst du dich.
— Saadi Schirazi zugeschrieben

occurrences.location: ru/wisdom-stories/how-we-treat-people.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
В отношениях с людьми держись так же, как у огня:
Отойдёшь слишком далеко — замёрзнешь. Подойдёшь слишком близко — обожжёшься.
— Приписывается Саади Ширази

occurrences.location: ky/wisdom-stories/how-we-treat-people.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Адамдар менен мамилең отко жакындагандай болсун:
Өтө алыстасаң — тоңосуң. Өтө жакындасаң — күйөсүң.
— Саади Ширазиге таандык деп айтылган накыл сөз

occurrences.location: az/wisdom-stories/human-being-emerged.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Düşüncəni qəlbə vurdum — sevgi alındı.
Sevginin üstünə əmək gəldim — vəfa alındı.
Çörəyi vicdanla böldüm — ədalət alındı.
Sevgini, əməyi, vicdanı, vəfanı və ədaləti topladım — insan alındı.
— Yaşar Kamala aid edilən sözlər

occurrences.location: en/wisdom-stories/human-being-emerged.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
I multiplied thought by heart—and the result was love.
I added effort to love—and the result was devotion.
I divided bread with conscience—and the result was justice.
I added love, effort, conscience, devotion, and justice—and the result was a human being.
— Attributed to Yaşar Kemal

occurrences.location: de/wisdom-stories/human-being-emerged.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Ich multiplizierte Gedanken mit Herz — daraus wurde Liebe.
Ich addierte Einsatz zur Liebe — daraus wurde Treue.
Ich teilte Brot nach meinem Gewissen — daraus wurde Gerechtigkeit.
Ich addierte Liebe, Einsatz, Gewissen, Treue und Gerechtigkeit — das Ergebnis war ein Mensch.
— Yaşar Kemal zugeschrieben

occurrences.location: ru/wisdom-stories/human-being-emerged.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Я умножил мысль на сердце — получилась любовь.
К любви прибавил труд — получилась верность.
Разделил хлеб по совести — получилась справедливость.
Сложил любовь, труд, совесть, верность и справедливость — получился человек.
— Приписывается Яшару Кемалю

occurrences.location: ky/wisdom-stories/human-being-emerged.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Ойду жүрөккө көбөйттүм — сүйүү жаралды.
Сүйүүгө эмгекти коштум — берилгендик жаралды.
Нанды абийир менен бөлүштүм — адилеттик жаралды.
Сүйүүнү, эмгекти, абийирди, берилгендикти жана адилеттикти коштум — адам жаралды.
— Яшар Кемалга таандык деп айтылган сөздөр

bölünərsək yox olarıq.

Sevgi var ikən nifrət niyə?
Barış var ikən savaş niyə?
Qardaşlıq var ikən didişmək niyə?

Dözüm var ikən dözümsüzlük niyə?

occurrences.exact_text:
Words attributed to Hacı Bektaş Veli:
Why hatred when there is love?
Why war when there is peace?
Why strife when there is brotherhood?
Why enmity when there is friendship?
Why intolerance when there is tolerance?
Why captivity when there is freedom?
Why injustice when there is justice?

occurrences.story_title: Warum Unrecht, wenn es Gerechtigkeit gibt?
occurrences.location: de/wisdom-stories/choose-justice.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Hacı Bektaş Veli zugeschriebene Worte:
Warum Hass, wenn es Liebe gibt?
Warum Krieg, wenn es Frieden gibt?
Warum Zwietracht, wenn es Brüderlichkeit gibt?
Warum Feindschaft, wenn es Freundschaft gibt?
Warum Intoleranz, wenn es Toleranz gibt?
Warum Gefangenschaft, wenn es Freiheit gibt?
Warum Unrecht, wenn es Gerechtigkeit gibt?

occurrences.location: ru/wisdom-stories/choose-justice.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Слова, приписываемые Хаджи Бекташу Вели:
Зачем ненависть, если есть любовь?
Зачем война, если есть мир?
Зачем раздоры, если есть братство?
Зачем вражда, если есть дружба?
Зачем нетерпимость, если есть терпимость?
Зачем неволя, если есть свобода?
Зачем несправедливость, если есть справедливость?

occurrences.story_title: Адилеттик барда адилетсиздиктин эмне кереги бар?

Сүйүү барда жек көрүүнүн эмне кереги бар?
Тынчтык барда согуштун эмне кереги бар?
Бир туугандык барда араздашуунун эмне кереги бар?
Достук барда душмандыктын эмне кереги бар?
Сабырдуулук барда сабырсыздыктын эмне кереги бар?
Эркиндик барда туткундуктун эмне кереги бар?
Адилеттик барда адилетсиздиктин эмне кереги бар?

occurrences.location: az/wisdom-stories/three-essentials-for-a-city.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Hər şəhərə üç şey lazımdır: kanalizasiya, hamam və kitabxana. Kanalizasiya şəhəri, hamam bədəni, kitabxana isə ruhu təmizləyir.
— Fateh Sultan Mehmedə aid edilən söz

occurrences.location: en/wisdom-stories/three-essentials-for-a-city.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Every city needs three things: a sewer system, a bathhouse, and a library. The sewer system cleanses the city, the bathhouse cleanses the body, and the library cleanses the soul.
— Attributed to Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror

occurrences.story_title: Drei Dinge, die eine Stadt braucht
occurrences.location: de/wisdom-stories/three-essentials-for-a-city.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Jede Stadt braucht drei Dinge: eine Kanalisation, ein Badehaus und eine Bibliothek. Die Kanalisation reinigt die Stadt, das Badehaus den Körper und die Bibliothek die Seele.
— Sultan Mehmed dem Eroberer zugeschrieben

occurrences.location: ru/wisdom-stories/three-essentials-for-a-city.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Каждому городу нужны три вещи: канализация, баня и библиотека. Канализация очищает город, баня — тело, а библиотека — душу.
— Приписывается султану Мехмеду Завоевателю

occurrences.location: ky/wisdom-stories/three-essentials-for-a-city.docx; attributed saying and credit
occurrences.exact_text:
Ар бир шаарга үч нерсе керек: канализация, мончо жана китепкана. Канализация шаарды, мончо денени, ал эми китепкана жан дүйнөнү тазалайт.
— Фатих Султан Мехмедге таандык деп айтылган сөз

title: Inserted Hajj verse has no source or adaptation label
finding: All five versions insert a four-line verse without a credit. The Azerbaijani wording closely follows a Turkish quatrain commonly attributed to Hacı Bektaş Veli in educational and cultural publications. The other versions freely adapt its final line, replacing Jerusalem and Mecca with general holy places and an explanation about inner work. This is understandable adaptation, but is not identified as such.
why: Readers cannot distinguish the borrowed verse from the site narrative or a literal translation. Modern attribution alone does not establish medieval authorship.
recommended_fix: Add a short note identifying this as an adaptation of the quatrain commonly attributed to Hacı Bektaş Veli, and identify the translator/adaptor if known. Confirm whether the freer final line is intentional. Retain qualified attribution unless an original textual source is supplied. Do not replace the story or change its identifier.

title: English apostrophes alternate between straight and typographic forms
finding: The complete title/body inventory finds straight internal apostrophes in 24 title or paragraph locations alongside typographic apostrophes in 573 locations. The straight forms include possessives in both headings and prose. This is typography, not a spelling or translation error.
why: Mixed apostrophe forms make the collection’s editorial presentation inconsistent.
recommended_fix: Use the existing predominant typographic apostrophe in the 24 listed reader-facing locations. Preserve identifiers, URLs, code and exact interface names. Synchronize the Word text and generated site only when corrections are authorized.

title: Judge tale gives an unverified precise setting without identifying its literary parallel
finding: The tale is explicitly qualified as a legend, but specifies Frankfurt in 1506. No contemporary record for that setting was established. Hebel’s Der kluge Richter, in the 1811 Schatzkästlein, contains the same false missing-money allegation and judicial resolution, with different amounts and an unspecified Eastern setting. This proves a textual parallel, not that Hebel originated the motif or that the site directly translated him.
why: A precise place and year can suggest documentary authenticity despite the legend qualifier, while readers are given no way to trace the related literary tale.
recommended_fix: Supply a record supporting Frankfurt/1506, or remove the unsupported precision and describe this as a retold traditional judge tale. Add a qualified comparison/source note to Hebel’s Der kluge Richter; do not assert exclusive authorship or silently replace the site’s amounts with Hebel’s.

Dindar və dürüst adam olan dülgər düşünür ki, bu qədər pul itirən şəxs mütləq onu axtaracaq. Kisəni sahibinə qaytarmaq üçün saxlayır.

title: Mercedes biography gives an unresolved remarriage-to-death interval
finding: The story states that Mercedes Jellinek’s second husband died a few months after their marriage. Secondary biographies disagree about the remarriage chronology; the audit has not located an independent marriage/death record resolving the interval. The supported brand dates and her death in 1929 at age thirty-nine are not being challenged.
why: An unqualified, precise biographical interval remains less secure than the surrounding manufacturer-supported history.
recommended_fix: Verify the interval against civil records or a documented biography. If that evidence is unavailable, omit only “a few months after their marriage” and retain the supported life summary. Do not substitute a competing year from an unsourced web account.

title: Historical anecdote details remain unverified despite appropriate legend framing
finding: The source research has not authenticated these particular episodes: Akşemseddin’s staged slap of Murad; Tarık Nusret’s son and morphine allocation; Yahya Efendi’s exact letter exchange; the original Cevdet Alkalp/Mustafa Doğru recollection; Fakir Baykurt’s original tea/lion memoir passage; Sinan’s deathbed water cutoff; Asad Pasha’s treasury dialogue; and the Zamzam sherbet practice. Existing legend or anecdote framing is acknowledged. Corroborating a person’s identity does not authenticate the dialogue. The original biographical passage behind the Howard Kelly milk anecdote also remains unverified; a secondary account citing Audrey Davis differs from the site’s opening circumstances. Henry Ford’s salt-and-waiter interview episode also lacks an authenticated historical source; secondary retellings assign the salt test to several different executives. The Russian and Kyrgyz Sinan titles state the disputed ending without the body’s explicit legend qualifier.
why: This is a documented limit of historical verification, not a finding that all ten stories are false. An editorial decision is needed about the evidentiary standard for named historical anecdotes.
recommended_fix: Decide to retain these as explicitly unverified retellings with short source-limit notes, or provide the original memoir, chronicle or archival reference for the episode. Keep qualifiers in every translation. Do not silently replace names from a different anecdote or describe these as proven historical incidents. Consider neutral or explicitly legendary RU/KY Sinan headings wherever titles appear without the introductory qualifier. For the Ford story, retain anecdote framing and do not turn the salt test into a validated recruitment technique.

occurrences.exact_text:
Qanuni Sultan Süleyman Osmanlı dövlətini dövrünün ən qüdrətli dövlətlərindən birinə çevirmişdi. Amma bəzən bir fikir onu narahat edirdi:
«Görəsən, gün gələr, Osmanlı dövləti də zəifləyib süqut edərmi?»
Rəvayətə görə, sultan bu narahatlığını süd qardaşı, elminə və mənəvi bəsirətinə güvəndiyi Yəhya Əfəndi ilə bölüşmək qərarına gəlir. Ona məktub yazır:
«Bir dövlət hansı halda çökər? Osmanlı dövlətinin də bir gün süquta uğraması mümkündürmü? Bu barədə fikrini bilmək istəyirəm».

occurrences.location: en/wisdom-stories/not-my-concern.docx; opening four body paragraphs (including attribution); corresponding site story
occurrences.exact_text:
Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent had made the Ottoman Empire one of the most powerful states of his time. Yet one thought sometimes troubled him:
“Could the Ottoman Empire one day weaken and fall?”
According to tradition, he decided to share his concern with Yahya Efendi, a respected scholar whose mother had also nursed Suleiman as a baby. The sultan trusted his learning and spiritual insight, and wrote to him:
“What causes a state to collapse? Could the Ottoman Empire itself fall one day? I would like to hear your thoughts.”

occurrences.location: de/wisdom-stories/not-my-concern.docx; opening four body paragraphs (including attribution); corresponding site story
occurrences.exact_text:
Sultan Süleyman der Prächtige hatte das Osmanische Reich zu einem der mächtigsten Staaten seiner Zeit gemacht. Doch manchmal beunruhigte ihn ein Gedanke:
„Könnte auch unser Reich eines Tages schwächer werden und untergehen?“
Der Überlieferung nach beschloss er, seine Sorge mit Yahya Efendi zu teilen. Der angesehene Gelehrte war sein Milchbruder: Yahyas Mutter hatte auch Süleyman als Säugling gestillt. Der Sultan vertraute seinem Wissen und seiner geistlichen Einsicht und schrieb ihm:
„Was bringt einen Staat zu Fall? Könnte eines Tages auch das Osmanische Reich untergehen? Ich möchte deine Gedanken dazu hören.“

occurrences.location: ru/wisdom-stories/not-my-concern.docx; opening four body paragraphs (including attribution); corresponding site story
occurrences.exact_text:
Сулейман Великолепный превратил Османскую державу в одно из самых могущественных государств своего времени. И всё же порой его тревожила мысль:
«Неужели однажды и наша держава может ослабеть и пасть?»
Согласно преданию, султан решил поделиться своей тревогой с молочным братом, учёным Яхьёй-эфенди, чьи знания и духовную прозорливость он высоко ценил. Он написал ему:
«Что приводит государство к гибели? Может ли однажды пасть и Османская держава? Хочу узнать твоё мнение».

occurrences.location: ky/wisdom-stories/not-my-concern.docx; opening four body paragraphs (including attribution); corresponding site story

«Бир күн келип, биздин мамлекет да алсырап, кулап калышы мүмкүнбү?»
Уламыш боюнча, султан бул тынчсыздануусун эмчектеш бир тууганы, билимине жана руханий көрөгөчтүгүнө ишенген аалым Яхья Эфенди менен бөлүшүүнү чечет. Ага кат жазат:

title: Respect moral leaves the staged slap unexplained
finding: The teacher and father arrange a demonstration in which the teacher slaps the father. The moral praises modelling respect and responsibility without distinguishing submission to a classroom rule from the physical humiliation used in the demonstration. The scene is explicitly staged; it is not a claim that the story directly instructs readers to hit anyone.
why: The central example can be read as equating respect with accepting a slap, which sits uneasily with the moral’s stated lesson about respectful conduct.
recommended_fix: Ask the author whether to retain the incident and clarify that the lesson concerns the father accepting the same rules as everyone else, not the slap. Alternatively, with approval, use a stern request to leave and knock again. Do not silently remove the scene during proofreading.

title: Traditional weight unit is unexplained in German and Russian
finding: English explains batman as a traditional weight unit. German uses Batman and Russian полбатмана without an explanation. Readers unfamiliar with the historical measure may not understand the quantity. This is a reader-accessibility suggestion, not a proven grammatical gender or numerical conversion error.
why: An unfamiliar measure interrupts comprehension; in German the spelling can also suggest the unrelated comic character.
recommended_fix: Add a brief first-use gloss: German “Batman (ein traditionelles Gewichtsmaß)” and Russian “батман — старинная мера веса”. Prefer a short explanatory note or natural rephrasing. Do not convert it to kilograms without a specified region and period.

title: Nails parable byline does not distinguish retelling from original plot authorship
finding: The story carries Etibar Siracsoy’s byline without an adaptation label. Its distinctive sequence—anger, nails driven into a fence, nails removed, remaining holes as wounds—also appears in independently published versions of the widely circulated parable. This does not establish who originated it, and is not a plagiarism allegation.
why: A bare byline can be read as credit for inventing the plot rather than for writing this particular retelling and moral.
recommended_fix: Ask the credited author to confirm the intended role. If this is a retelling, retain the name with a label such as “retold by” and identify a source if known; keep the added moral separate. Do not remove the credit or assign another author without evidence.

title: Kyrgyz ending substitutes a stronger maxim for the source moral
finding: The Kyrgyz moral ends “Бирок баштан өткөрүлбөгөн сүйүү да — жоготуу.” (“But love not experienced is also a loss.”). The Azerbaijani source instead explains that fear of a possible separation deprives someone of the opportunity for closeness and joy. The plot remains recognizable, but this is an interpretive adaptation. In the dialogue, the second imagined accusation also changes smiling at someone to staring at someone.
why: The comparison view presents the versions as the same story. Readers receive a more categorical concluding claim and lose the source’s explicit contrast between avoiding possible separation and missing possible closeness.
recommended_fix: Confirm whether the freer Kyrgyz ending is intentional. For closer alignment, use “Сабак: Кээде адам баштала элек сүйүүнүн бүтүшүнөн коркот. Мүмкүн болгон ажырашуудан өзүн коргойм деп, жакындыкты жана кубанычты сезүү мүмкүнчүлүгүнөн да куру калат.” In the dialogue, replace “муну эмнеге тиктедиң?” with “буга эмнеге жылмайдың?” if strict alignment is desired.

title: Samurai parable has an identifiable published parallel but no source note
finding: The samurai, provoking warrior, pupils and rejected-gift explanation closely parallel the story published on Paulo Coelho’s own blog. An older related analogy appears in the Akkosa Sutta (SN 7.2), with different characters and setting. The site labels this a samurai parable but does not identify the source used for this retelling.
why: Readers cannot distinguish the traditional motif from the modern samurai adaptation. The parallel does not establish copying, exclusive authorship, or the source actually used by the compiler.
recommended_fix: Ask the compiler which version was used. Add a concise “retold/adapted from” note if Coelho’s version was the source; otherwise identify the actual source and optionally note the older related motif. Do not automatically credit Coelho as inventor of the underlying analogy.

title: Punctuation-loss parable needs an adaptation/source note
finding: All five versions use the distinctive sequence of a person losing punctuation and ending with only other people’s thoughts inside quotation marks. A closely corresponding piece, «Знаки препинания», is published under Alexander Kanevsky’s name in Trud (2002) and on his Proza.ru page (2016). The site adds a separate period-loss episode and rewrites the explanations, so it is not a literal translation.
why: The absent source note prevents readers from distinguishing the published literary parallel from the compiler’s adaptation. These sources do not establish which intermediary version the compiler used.
recommended_fix: Confirm the source used by the compiler. If based on Kanevsky’s piece, add a localized “adapted from Alexander Kanevsky, Знаки препинания” note and identify the edition. Preserve the distinction between adaptation and quotation; do not silently label this an anonymous traditional proverb.

title: Water’s fire-extinguishing property is stated without qualification
finding: In a list explicitly presented as properties of water, all five versions state that water puts out fire when it meets it. Unlike the later heart metaphor, this is presented as a physical property without limits. Water is unsuitable for some fires; OSHA specifically warns against water on grease and electrical fires.
why: The broad claim is factually misleading and could be remembered as a general safety rule, even though this is a moral essay rather than firefighting guidance.
recommended_fix: Narrow the example without expanding the story into a safety manual: e.g. AZ “Odun alovunu söndürə bilər.”; EN “It can extinguish burning wood.”; DE “Es kann brennendes Holz löschen.”; RU “Может погасить горящую древесину.”; KY “Күйүп жаткан жыгачты өчүрө алат.” Confirm the preferred wording and preserve the surrounding water/heart analogy.
